fatal_errors: The proposed precursor pretreatment and nominally single-phase ZrB2 route misses the target intervention: adding 30% AlFeNiCoCr high-entropy-alloy binder and optimizing SPS at 1300–1600 °C.
The service environment is incorrectly changed from molten aluminum at 700 °C for 4–12 days to an unspecified plating bath at 200 °C for 1000 hours.
Neither cited source supports dense single-phase ZrB2 made by the proposed route, improved mechanical integrity, or resistance to long-duration liquid-bath penetration.
The hypothesis omits the central temperature-dependent binder behavior: pore filling and grain bonding at 1500 °C versus binder overflow and renewed porosity at 1600 °C.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad goals of reducing processing temperature, densifying the material, and limiting liquid infiltration through pores. Its proposed intervention, however, is scientifically distinct from the target and is not adequately supported by the cited evidence. E1 describes precursor processing and pyrolysis for high-entropy boride powders, while E2 describes mechanically alloyed high-entropy diborides SPS-consolidated at 2000 °C; neither establishes the claimed production or service performance of pure ZrB2. The arbitrary 200 °C bath also fails to test the relevant molten-Al corrosion mechanism. The experiment has a useful same-route pretreatment control and several relevant measurements, but it lacks bath chemistry, target-condition controls, quantitative porosity/corrosion metrics, and direct comparison among SPS temperatures. Thus it is falsifiable in a general sense but cannot reconstruct or rigorously test the target hypothesis.
